mekayis.metin:
(زَجَلَ) الزَّاءُ وَالْجِيمُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الرَّمْيِ بِالشَّيْءِ وَالدَّفْعِ لَهُ. يُقَالُ قَبَّحَ اللَّهُ أُمًّا زَجَلَتْ بِهِ. وَالزَّجْلُ: إِرْسَالُ الْحَمَامِ الْهَادِي. وَالْمِزْجَلُ: الْمِزْرَاقُ. وَزَجَلَ الْفَحْلُ، إِذَا أَلْقَى مَاءَهُ فِي الرَّحِمِ. وَيُقَالُ إِنَّ الزَّاجَلَ: مَاءُ الظَّلِيمِ ; لِأَنَّهُ يَزْجُلُ بِهِ. قَالَ ابْنُ أَحْمَرَ:
وَمَا بَيْضَاتُ ذِي لِبَدٍ هِجَفٍّ ... سُقِينَ بِزَاجَلٍ حَتَّى رَوِينَا
وَيُقَالُ بَلِ الزَّاجَلُ مُخُّ الْبِيضِ، وَالْأَوَّلُ أَقْيَسُ.
وَمِمَّا شَذَّ عَنِ الْبَابِ الزُّجْلَةُ: الْقِطْعَةُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَجَمْعُهَا زُجَلٌ. وَالزِّئْجِيلُ: الرَّجُلُ الضَّعِيفُ. وَمِنْ هَذَا، إِنْ كَانَ صَحِيحًا، الزَّاجَلُ: حَلْقَةٌ تَكُونُ فِي طَرَفِ حَبْلِ الثِّقَلِ.

zemahseri.hakikat: " للملائكة زجل بالتسبيح ". وزجله بالحربة وزجه بها: رماه. وخرج الأمير وبين يديه الرجالة والزجالة. ولعن الله أما زجلت به ونجلت. وزجل الحمام الهادي: أرسله زجلاً.

to repel; to spear s.o.’: † zaǧala . – Cf. also † zāǧil ‘peg of a water-skin; ring on the butt of a spear; leader of an army’, † zaǧǧālaẗ ‘archers’, † mizǧal ‘spear-head; short spear’, † mizǧāl ‘wooden arrow’; ▪ † ZǦL_4 ‘condition, state; party of people; little quantity’: † zuǧlaẗ ▪ [gnrl] : DRS 8 (1999) #ZGL distinguishes eight values in Sem, of which only the first three are represented in Ar, and only in Ar. – HDAL lists some Gz and Amh items as cognates belonging somehow to Ar √ZǦL, without however specifying to exactly which of the attested values. – DRS hesitates to regard [v1] ‘to let go, release’ and † [v3] † zāǧil ‘peg of a water-skin’ (= DRS #ZGL-2 ‘cheville…’) as belonging together, and so also [v2] *‘to be loud, make noise’ and ( DRS #ZGL-4) the Aram items nSyr zāgil ‘to deceive’ and Ṭur zagál ‘sly, treacherous’. ▪ [gnrl] : It seems that, for the etymology of the Ar items, we may disregard DRS values #ZGL-4–8, for several reasons: a) #ZGL-1–3 are specific to Ar and – for the moment, at least – do not show clear semantic overlapping with any of #ZGL-4–8; b) within Ar, a plausible hypothesis for semantic development can be imagined: we may assume *[v1] ‘to let go, release, bring forth’ as primary value and derive the others (except † [v4]) from it as follows: [v2] as *‘to release a sound, produce noise > to produce stunning rhymes > zajal poetry’ and † [v3] as *‘to release an arrow, launch a spear, etc., open a water-skin by removing the peg’. – Cf. also † zāǧil ‘peg of a water-skin ( )’; similarly: † zāǧil in the sense of ‘ring on the butt of a spear (*what releases the spear)’, † mizǧal ‘spear-head; short spear’ and † mizǧāl ‘wooden arrow’ (both orig. n.instr.), and † zaǧǧālaẗ (pl.) ‘archers (*those who release arrows)’. DRS also mentions the use of zaǧala as † ‘to inject, ejaculate’ and † zāǧal (var. zaʔǧal ) ‘sperm’. ▪ [v1] : According to the hypothesis sketched in the preceding paragraph, [v1] ‘to let go, release’ is the primary value in the Ar root from which at least [v2] and † [v3] can be derived as semantic extensions/specifications. ▪ [v2] : The specific use of zaǧal as a kind of popular poetry is based on a more general meaning ‘shouting, raising one’s voice, being noisy’, itself from *‘to release a sound’, preserved in several ClassAr lexemes, like † zaǧila ( a , zaǧal ) ‘to be cheerful; to raise the voice; to play’, † zaǧlaẗ (pl. zaǧalāt ) ‘confused voices, shouts’, or † zaǧil ‘rustling (plant); noisy company; thundering (cloud)’. According to Schoeler and Stoetzer, »in its non-technical meaning« zaǧal means »‘voice, sound or cry, trilling or quavering of the voice’ (Lane). […] In poetry, [it is the term for] a genre in Muslim Spain, written only in the Arabic dialect of Spain. Its most frequent rhyme scheme is aa bbb a ccc a , that is, the rhyme scheme of a Musammat with introductory lines; in present-day Arabic, za dj al may denote various types of dialect poems, even those with monorhyme« – » Zadjal «, in EI² , Glossary and Index of Terms . For further details, see, e.g., art. » Zadjal « (G. Schoeler and W. Stoetzer), in EI² . – Dolgopolsky2012 #2025 thinks Ar zaǧila ( swei̪gʰ|g̑ʰl- ~ * swigʰ|g̑ʰl- ‘to produce sound by blowing’) and Uralic languages (Vogul, Ostyakish) and reconstructs Nostr * śûyg˅ļ˅ ‘to produce sounds by voice or by blowing’. † [v3] : While [v2] signifies the *‘releasing of sound or noise’, † [v3] comprises the *‘releasing’ of other things, such as pigeons, sperm, pegs, arrows, spears, etc. † [v4] : The many values given in Hava1899 for the n.f. † zuǧlaẗ – ‘condition, state’, ‘party of people’, ‘little quantity’ – are hard to relate to the primary value of *‘releasing’. Probably, they represent some very specific usage. For the time being, however, their etymology remains rather obscure. – For ‘party of people’ one could think of a lit. meaning of *‘group producing (= releasing) unspecific noise, confused voices’, thus akin to [v2]. – ▪ [gnrl] : [ HDAL and] DRS 8 (1999) ZGL- 1 Ar zaǧala ‘lancer, faire partir (un pigeon), pousser en dehors; injecter, éjaculer’, zaʔǧal , zāǧal ‘sperme’, zāǧal ‘lance courte, javelot’. - ? 2 zāǧila ‘cheville avec laquelle on resserre la corde de fermeture d’un sac’. - 3 zaǧila ‘faire du bruit, chanter, murmurer, bourdonner’, zaǧal ‘clameur’; HispAr zagál ‘chanter; chanson’. - ? 4 nSyr zāgil ‘tromper’, Ṭur zagál ‘sournois, perfide’. - 5 nSyr zīgil ‘bouton, protubérance (sur une coquille)’. - 6 Gz zāgʷal , Amh zagʷäl , zagol ‘coquillage marin’ [ HDAL : dto. ‘mother of pearl’]. - 7 Amh zaggʷälä ‘devenir sale, changer de poil (bête)’ [ HDAL : Amh zägägʷälä ~ zaggʷälä ‘to become white, become blue’], zägäle ‘agneau un peu grandi’ [ HDAL : Amh zägäle ~ zägale ‘ram, male sheep’]. - 8 Tña zägälä ‘abattre (bête de boucherie), lacérer; mutiler (animal à qui on coupe l’oreille par exemple)’. ▪ [v2] : Dolgopolsky2012 #2025 juxtaposes Ar zaǧila ‘to sing, speak loudly, (of several persons) produce noise by laughing and speaking loudly’ with (NaIE:) Got swiglōn ‘Flöte blasen’, oHGe swëgala ‘flute, pipe (Schwegel, Flöte, Pfeife, Orgelpfeife), Rohr’, […] nHGe Schwegel ‘fife, flute’, AngSax (= oEngl) sweʒel ‘music’, sweʒl-horn ‘trumpet horn’ as well as some (Uralic > Finno-Ugrian >) Vogul and Ostyakish terms. ▪ … ▪ DRS 8 (1999), comm. on #ZGL 1 - 3 : comp.
